title: Audit log ledger: adaptive partitioning, tiered retention, and cost-aware ingest throttles
creator: Priya Patel
description:
Problem: Current audit ingestion writes every event to a single hot index with full JSON bodies retained for 365 days. Costs have spiked ~2.8x YTD and query latencies for admin investigations are inconsistent. We need an ingestion and storage strategy that meets compliance (configurable retention per customer), preserves forensic integrity for investigations, and reduces storage/query costs.

Goal: Build an "adaptive ledger" for audit logs that partitions by event shape and time, performs TTL-driven compaction (full payload -> hashed pointer), supports tiered hot/cold storage, and applies cost-aware backpressure at ingest. Non-goals: changing audit schema or removing mandatory fields required for compliance (actor, timestamp, action, resource).
acceptance_criteria: Configurable retention windows per org tier via Console (e.g., 90d full, 365d compact) exposed in admin settings
Ingest path partitions events by 'event_profile' and day and writes to hot index for configurable hot-window
Compaction job converts older documents to compacted form (payload replaced with SHA256 pointer and encrypted blob in cold store) without changing event metadata for queries
Backpressure mechanism limits sustained ingest above defined token rate and emits throttling metrics and errors to callers
Cost impact: projected storage reduction >= 30% for average production workload; query latency on hot window <= 250ms p95
End-to-end tests covering ingest -> compaction -> restore-of-record (for investigation flow)
implementation_notes:
High-level decisions:
- Partitioning: primary partition key = org_id:event_profile (profile derived from schema fingerprint), secondary = date (YYYY-MM-DD). This allows efficient deletes/TTL and per-org queries.
- Hot window: default 30d in SSD-backed indices with full payloads; cold window: older data compacted into object store (Parquet + encrypted blobs).
- Compaction: daily compaction job reads candidate docs > hot_window and replaces 'payload' with {type:'compact', pointer:sha256, location:s3://...} and writes encrypted full-event to cold store. Metadata (actor, ts, action, resource, event_profile) kept unmodified for query.
- Forensics: reverse-lookup service supports restoring a compacted record on-demand given pointer; restoration logs all accesses for audit.
- Backpressure: ingest-proxy implements a token-bucket per-tenant with horizon burst; when exceeded we respond 429 with Retry-After and emit metric ingest.throttle.{org_id}.
- Indexing: store per-partition inverted index for fields used by Console queries (actor, action, resource, request_id). Use a bloom-filter postfix to avoid expensive cold-store fetches for common queries.
- Cost controls: daily job estimates projected 30-45% saving via compaction + cold-store transitions; tagging of cold objects with org_id + retention policy for lifecycle rules.

Trade-offs considered:
- Keeping full JSON in hot store speeds investigations but increases cost; chosen hybrid keeps metadata hot and payload cold after window.
- Real-time analytics vs compaction latency: compaction is asynchronous (batch) to avoid affecting ingest tail latency.

Open questions:
- Legal: acceptable minimum retention of full payloads by region (asked Legal on 2026-02-25).
- SLO for restore latency (target 5s) needs sign-off from Compliance and Support teams.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature-flag behind 'adaptive-audit-ledger' at org level; default OFF for existing orgs
2) Enable for internal orgs + small beta customers (10 orgs) to gather metrics
3) Monitor metrics for 2 weeks; iterate on compaction thresholds and hot-window sizing
4) Gradual ramp to all orgs after automated migration verification
5) Release Console UI controls for admin retention and rollout announcement
test_plan: Unit tests for partition key derivation, compaction logic, and pointer lookup
Integration test: synthesize 120d of events, run compaction, validate query results and restore flow
Chaos test: simulate spike ingest at 5x baseline to validate token-bucket throttling and graceful degradation
E2E Canary: enable for single org and verify dashboards, alerting, and cost telemetry
monitoring_and_alerting: Dashboards: Audit-Ingest: ingest-rate, p50/p95/p99 latency, throttle-rate by org
Storage: hot-index-size per org, cold-store object count, daily compaction throughput
Alerts: throttle-rate > 0.5% for 1h (P1), compaction job failure (P0), restore latency > 10s (P1)
review_feedback: Liam O'Connor (SRE): prefer incremental compaction streams to avoid large read spikes; suggest streaming-based compaction using existing changefeed
Aisha Khan (Security): require HSM-backed keys for cold-store encryption and per-org KMS keys; ensure pointer values are non-guessable
Dana Moore (Product): add Console UX to display 'full payload available until {date}' and an investigator restore button
Ravi Shah (Legal): confirm region-specific retention limits; requested updated policy matrix by 2026-03-05
status_updates: 2026-02-19 - Priya Patel: RFC posted to Confluence; initial partitioning prototype landed in ingest-proxy branch 'audit-ledger/prototype'.
2026-02-28 - Miguel Santos: Implemented token-bucket per-tenant; integration tests for throttling added (PR #256).
2026-03-02 - Miguel Santos: Compaction worker PoC completed; uses batched GETs + bulk writes to cold store. Observed 40% reduction on synthetic dataset.
2026-03-08 - Priya Patel: Legal confirmed EU minimum full-payload retention = 30 days. Adjusted default hot-window for EU orgs to 30d.
2026-03-12 - Miguel Santos: Canary enabled for 'internal-beta' orgs; initial metrics show hot-index size down 22% after 7 days. No customer-visible errors.
estimated_cost_savings: 30-45% storage + 10-20% query cost reduction (estimates from 30d hot window + compaction)
migration_plan: Run dry-run compaction for each org to estimate storage delta and surface any missing dependencies
Migrate orgs in waves grouped by size (small -> medium -> large) and region
Expose migration status in Console with rollback options for 7 days after migration
Support: enable manual restore for on-call to fetch original payloads for 30 days post-migration
rollback_plan: If compaction job regresses queries or causes restore failures: disable compaction via feature-flag and trigger backfill to restore full payloads from cold-store snapshots (takes up to 24h for large orgs)
If ingest throttling incorrectly blocks majority traffic: revert token-bucket limits and re-run canary with lower thresholds
